database_summary: Small clinical dataset with three tables: Patient (one row per patient, descriptive/demographic), Examination (multiple examination records per patient with clinical categorizations and some binary/enum test results), and Laboratory (many dated laboratory measurements per patient; repeated measurements over time). The schema links Examination.ID -> Patient.ID and Laboratory.ID -> Patient.ID. Laboratory has a composite primary key of (ID, Date) indicating time series measurements. Examination rows are events/visits/examinations. Patient holds mostly stable descriptive attributes. Joins from Patient to Examination are 1-to-many; joins from Patient to Laboratory are 1-to-many and can multiply when combining Examination and Laboratory unless keyed/filtered by date.)

accepted.name: patient_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday,
  "Description",
  "First Date",
  Admission,
  Diagnosis
FROM
  Patient
accepted.description: Normalized patient-level projection exposing stable demographic and identifying columns. Use this as the patient entity when joining to facts or computing per-patient aggregates. | Use for: List patients by demographic attributes (SEX, Birthday range); Join patient info to latest lab or examination; Aggregate counts of patients by Admission or Diagnosis

accepted.name: examination_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "aCL IgG",
  "aCL IgM",
  ANA,
  "ANA Pattern",
  "aCL IgA",
  Diagnosis,
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  Symptoms,
  Thrombosis
FROM
  Examination
accepted.description: One row per clinical Examination event for a patient, exposing examination date, test results, diagnosis and binary flags. Use this to filter cohorts by examination attributes or to join to patient-level data. | Use for: Find examinations with thrombosis or specific symptom/diagnosis; Trend of aCL/ANA measures across examinations; Count examinations per patient or filter by exam date ranges

accepted.name: lab_latest_per_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  GOT,
  GPT,
  LDH,
  ALP,
  TP,
  ALB,
  UA,
  UN,
  CRE,
  "T-BIL",
  "T-CHO",
  TG,
  CPK,
  GLU,
  WBC,
  RBC,
  HGB,
  HCT,
  PLT,
  PT,
  APTT,
  FG,
  PIC,
  TAT,
  TAT2,
  "U-PRO",
  IGG,
  IGA,
  IGM,
  CRP,
  RA,
  RF,
  C3,
  C4,
  RNP,
  SM,
  SC170,
  SSA,
  SSB,
  CENTROMEA,
  DNA,
  "DNA-II",
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) AS lab_row_rank
FROM
  Laboratory
accepted.description: Latest Laboratory record per patient based on Date. Exposes a row_number rank and returns the most recent lab row (rank = 1) when filtered downstream. Useful for snapshotting current lab state per patient. | Use for: Get latest lab snapshot per patient (WHERE lab_row_rank = 1); Ranked lab history queries (top-K recent lab dates per patient)

accepted.name: examination_counts_per_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  COUNT(*) AS exam_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Thrombosis IS NOT NULL AND Thrombosis != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS thrombosis_count,
  MIN("Examination Date") AS first_exam_date,
  MAX("Examination Date") AS last_exam_date
FROM
  Examination
GROUP BY
  ID
accepted.description: Per-patient aggregate counts and basic summary of examinations: total number of examinations and number of examinations with Thrombosis flagged. Useful for patient-level risk summaries. | Use for: Count examinations per patient; Identify patients with any thrombosis events; Find patients' first and last examination dates

accepted.name: lab_aggregates_per_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  AVG(GOT) AS avg_GOT,
  MIN(GOT) AS min_GOT,
  MAX(GOT) AS max_GOT,
  AVG(GPT) AS avg_GPT,
  MIN(GPT) AS min_GPT,
  MAX(GPT) AS max_GPT,
  AVG(LDH) AS avg_LDH,
  MIN(LDH) AS min_LDH,
  MAX(LDH) AS max_LDH,
  AVG(ALP) AS avg_ALP,
  MIN(ALP) AS min_ALP,
  MAX(ALP) AS max_ALP,
  AVG(WBC) AS avg_WBC,
  MIN(WBC) AS min_WBC,
  MAX(WBC) AS max_WBC,
  AVG(HGB) AS avg_HGB,
  MIN(HGB) AS min_HGB,
  MAX(HGB) AS max_HGB,
  AVG(PLT) AS avg_PLT,
  MIN(PLT) AS min_PLT,
  MAX(PLT) AS max_PLT
FROM
  Laboratory
GROUP BY
  ID
accepted.description: Per-patient aggregated laboratory measures (mean, min, max) for common numeric labs. Use this when comparing typical lab levels between patients or cohorts. Columns with non-numeric types are omitted from numeric aggregation. | Use for: Compare average lab values across patients or groups; Identify outlier patients by max/min lab values; Use aggregated lab features for modeling or cohort selection

accepted.name: patient_with_latest_lab
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  p.SEX,
  p.Birthday,
  p."Description",
  p."First Date",
  p.Admission,
  p.Diagnosis,
  l.Date AS lab_Date,
  l.GOT,
  l.GPT,
  l.LDH,
  l.ALP,
  l.TP,
  l.ALB,
  l.WBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.PLT,
  l.CRP,
  l."DNA-II"
FROM
  patient_core p
  LEFT JOIN lab_latest_per_patient l ON p.ID = l.ID AND l.lab_row_rank = 1
accepted.description: Denormalized patient-level snapshot that joins Patient to their latest Laboratory record. This references lab_latest_per_patient and is useful for queries needing patient demographics plus current lab values. | Use for: Patient snapshot reports combining demographics and latest lab; Filter patients by current abnormal lab values; Create cohorts using both demographic and latest lab features

accepted.name: exams_with_same_day_lab
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.ID,
  e."Examination Date",
  e."aCL IgG",
  e."aCL IgM",
  e.ANA,
  e."ANA Pattern",
  e."aCL IgA",
  e.Diagnosis AS Examination_Diagnosis,
  e.KCT,
  e.RVVT,
  e.LAC,
  e.Symptoms,
  e.Thrombosis,
  l.Date AS Lab_Date,
  l.GOT,
  l.GPT,
  l.LDH,
  l.ALP,
  l.TP,
  l.ALB,
  l.WBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.PLT
FROM
  Examination e
  JOIN Laboratory l ON e.ID = l.ID AND e."Examination Date" = l.Date
accepted.description: Join Examination events to Laboratory records that occurred on the exact same date for the same patient. Use when you need lab context taken concurrently with an examination. Avoids explosion by requiring exact date equality. | Use for: Analyze lab values at the time of an examination; Compare exam findings with same-day lab measures; Select examination events that had concurrent lab tests

accepted.name: lab_running_avg_by_patient
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  WBC,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date) AS seq_num,
  AVG(WBC) OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_avg_WBC
FROM
  Laboratory
accepted.description: Running (cumulative) average of a numeric lab (example: WBC) per patient ordered by Date. Exposes running_avg_WBC and a row_number to allow downstream filtering to particular points in the series. Use for trend or longitudinal feature engineering. | Use for: Longitudinal trend of WBC per patient; Compute features like moving averages or detect shifts over time

accepted.name: patients_with_exams_and_lab_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID,
  COALESCE(e.exam_count, 0) AS exam_count,
  COALESCE(l.lab_count, 0) AS lab_count
FROM
  Patient p
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS exam_count FROM Examination GROUP BY ID
  ) e ON p.ID = e.ID
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS lab_count FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID
  ) l ON p.ID = l.ID
accepted.description: Per-patient counts of examinations and laboratory records as a compact pivot-style summary (one row per patient). Useful for cohort filtering by data availability or for joins where you need counts of each fact type. | Use for: Filter patients by having at least one exam or lab; Summarize data availability per patient; Join counts as features for downstream modeling

accepted.name: patients_with_recent_exam_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  "Examination Date",
  "aCL IgG",
  "aCL IgM",
  ANA,
  "ANA Pattern",
  "aCL IgA",
  Diagnosis,
  KCT,
  RVVT,
  LAC,
  Symptoms,
  Thrombosis,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY "Examination Date" DESC) AS exam_row_rank
FROM
  Examination
accepted.description: Ranks Examination rows per patient by Examination Date descending to identify the most recent examinations. Exposes exam_row_rank so downstream filters can pick the latest exam (exam_row_rank = 1) or top-K recent exams. | Use for: Get each patient's most recent examination; Retrieve top-K recent examinations per patient
